fullAnalysis: Pinpoint #488 starts in a slightly tricky place because Cup and Bank can pull you toward sports, money, or international institutions. Then Map and Record widen the field even more. The board feels mixed until you stop asking what topic connects the clues and instead test whether the same word can sit in front of every one of them.

My first read tried to build a world-affairs category from Cup and Bank, but that idea starts to wobble when Map and Record show up beside them. The better pivot is to treat the clues as half-finished phrases. World Cup lands immediately, and after that World Bank, world map, and world record all follow without strain. The last clue, Wide Web, is the giveaway that confirms the pattern is not thematic at all but phrase-based.

This puzzle stays clean because each clue forms a familiar expression with the same leading word. World Cup is the international tournament, the World Bank is the global financial institution, a world map shows the whole planet, and a world record marks the best known achievement in a category. World Wide Web finishes the set with the most explicit version of the same connector.

That is why the answer to LinkedIn Pinpoint #488 is Words that follow "World". Once you test the same prefix across all five clues, the board changes from a messy mix of subjects into one straightforward language puzzle.

wordHints.Cup: World Cup is the international championship tournament most people recognize from soccer and other sports.
wordHints.Bank: The World Bank is the global financial institution that makes this clue fit the same phrase pattern.
wordHints.Map: A world map shows the whole Earth, so map becomes another natural phrase after world.
wordHints.Record: A world record is the best known performance or achievement in a particular event or category.
wordHints.Wide Web: World Wide Web is the full phrase, making this the clearest confirmation clue on the board.

lessons: Switch from topic-hunting to phrase-testing when the board spreads across unrelated domains. Cup, Bank, Map, and Record become much easier once you treat them as incomplete expressions.
Use the strongest phrase as your anchor. World Cup is common enough to test quickly, and once it works, the rest of the board becomes easier to evaluate.
Expect one clue to make the pattern obvious at the end. Wide Web is the sort of clue that confirms the board was built around a shared word rather than a shared subject.

faqs.question: What is the answer to LinkedIn Pinpoint #488?
faqs.answer: The answer is Words that follow "World". The clues form World Cup, World Bank, world map, world record, and World Wide Web.

faqs.question: Why does Wide Web matter so much in #488?
faqs.answer: Because World Wide Web is such a complete and familiar phrase that it confirms the board is about words that follow world, not about one broad category like geography or global affairs.

faqs.question: Could Map have pointed to geography instead?
faqs.answer: On its own, yes. But once World Cup and World Bank are already in play, world map fits much more cleanly as part of the same phrase pattern.

faqs.question: How should I approach phrase puzzles like #488?
faqs.answer: When the clues seem to live in different subjects, try adding one short common word before or after each clue. If several familiar phrases appear at once, you are usually on the right track.
